item.title: 2024 NALA Application is Now Open
item.description:
2024 NALA Application is Now Open!

 

Apply for the New American Leadership Academy 

We are pleased to share with you that the application for the 2024 New American Leadership Academy (NALA) cohort is now available.

NALA is an opportunity for New American professionals to foster their personal development by building knowledge in civic engagement, and discovering new ways to contribute to their respective communities and the city of Columbus at large.  Academy participants receive mentorship and professional development on topics including government, civic engagement, and strategic collaboration along with  implicit bias training, public speaking, and conflict resolution and management. The bi-monthly sessions will begin in March 2024 and end in November 2024.

Applications will be accepted now through November 17, 2023. For more information, and to apply online, please visit www.columbus.gov/nala.

item.title: Opportunity City: Welcome to Fall, Columbus!
item.description:
Happy Fall, Columbus!

As I reflect on a fantastic summer, I am grateful for all of the great activities our city had to offer, including packed festivals, concerts at the Columbus Commons and, perhaps most notably, over $20 million in direct support for summer youth programming. But the arrival of fall does not mean the fun is over. I look forward to our final Rise Up! CBUS in the Hilltop tomorrow, Sept. 28, and CelebrateOne’s First Birthday Party on Saturday, Oct. 7 – with many more exciting events coming down the pike. Be sure to follow my Facebook, Instagram and X accounts for regular updates on opportunities to stay connected and involved across the community.

Sincerely,

Mayor Andy Ginther

Summer programming keeps youth safe

Summer camps and programs serve as safe, constructive outlets for youth to learn, grow and develop. This summer, the City of Columbus devoted $20.1 million toward keeping teens and kids engaged, preparing them for future careers, and helping them to get outside and play— all while keeping their minds sharp in preparation for the new school year. According to the latest count, our summer programming reached over 15,000 participants.

Summer programs are also a reliable way to connect kids with nutritious meals. I am proud to share that our Go Lunch! program served over 240,800 meals.

We have an obligation to invest in every person who calls Columbus home – particularly our young people. And we owe it to our future leaders to provide them with the skills and knowledge they need to lay the groundwork for a lifetime of success.

New affordable apartments replace abandoned music venue

Last week, I celebrated the opening of The Sinclair apartments with the Columbus Metropolitan Housing Authority, NRP Group, the Ohio Housing Financing Agency, Huntington National Bank and State Senator Hearcel Craig. These 180 high-quality, affordable apartments mark a major milestone in my Columbus Housing Strategy, our blueprint for building the housing we need while including everyone in our region’s prosperity.

At the end of the day, no resident should have to spend more than 30 percent of their income to live in safe housing in a neighborhood of their choice. And a family earning $50,000 a year should be able to choose where their family lives. By working with our partners across the region, I’m confident we’ll make this aspiration a reality for our city.

Congratulations to our rising stars in the Division of Fire

I applaud the 47 Columbus Division of Fire graduates for stepping up and committing themselves to one of our city’s most essential, dynamic and respected professions. I also commend our 3rd Fire Cadet Class, a program I started with former Fire Chief and Public Safety Director Ned Pettus to increase diversity so that our firefighters better reflect the communities they serve.

We also welcome K9 firefighter teams Jeremy Thoma and Labrador, Harry; and State Fire Marshal Jeff Koehn and Labrador, Harley. These teams will join the arson detection division, specializing in detecting 10 different liquids commonly used to start arson fires.

item.title: Opportunity City: Keep Cool Columbus
item.description:
Hello, Columbus!

Summertime means gathering with family and friends, engaging with your fellow neighbors and communities, and enjoying the many wonderful festivities our city has to offer. I am thankful to Columbus Police and Fire for keeping our major events safe, helping to manage traffic and roadway closures, connecting with our youth, promoting heat and fire safety, and so much more. Thanks to our city’s comprehensive approach to neighborhood safety – which includes prevention, intervention and enforcement strategies – we’ve had a safe and successful festival season. But summer is not over yet. We will continue to be diligent and proactive in keeping Columbus safe – today and every day.

Sincerely,

Mayor Andy Ginther

First Lady Dr. Jill Biden visits Columbus

Earlier this month, I had the great honor of joining First Lady Dr. Jill Biden for the launch of the Columbus Workforce Hub alongside Congresswoman Beatty, Columbus City Council, local education leaders and our business partners.  

Columbus, if you haven’t already heard, is among five cities selected by the Biden-Harris Administration for the Investing in America Workforce initiative, which focuses on bringing together higher education, employers, unions, high schools and other stakeholders to build a diverse and skilled workforce. Our selection for the workforce hub is thanks, in part, to recent investments from Intel and Honda – solidifying our region’s standing at the forefront of semiconductor manufacturing, clean energy, biotechnology, high-performance computing and transportation innovation.

Congratulations to our 141st police recruit class

I applaud the 34 newest recruits of the Columbus Division of Police for stepping forward at a time when leadership and integrity have never been more vital to the safety and security of our neighborhoods. So far, we have graduated 63 recruits this year and expect two additional recruit classes to graduate by the end of 2023. After graduation, these new officers will undergo 15 weeks of field training alongside experienced Field Training Officers. My goal is to have more police officers and firefighters on the streets of Columbus by the end of 2024 than ever before, and the addition of these recruits is an important step forward in those efforts.

Dive into the brand new Glenwood Pool

Swimming is a summertime staple, and Columbus pools are great places for children and families to keep cool, stay active and have fun. The City of Columbus now has eight incredible outdoor pools – two of which were fully remodeled this year. One of the new pools is Glenwood Pool, located at 1888 Fairmont Avenue. The pool offers swimmers dual water slides, a dedicated diving pool, an eight-lane lap pool, a kiddie pool, a pool house and sheltered and shaded recreation areas. You can learn more about pool locations, hours and classes here.

Check out the new Columbus.gov

The City of Columbus has launched a new, fresh and innovative design on our website, Columbus.gov. This new website features a modern look and feel, improved mobile compatibility and enhanced search functionality. The new Columbus.gov has been structured so that our residents can access the resources they need in a faster, more efficient way – dramatically reducing digital barriers and ensuring that everyone has a better experience when engaging with their local government.  

The transition from the old website to the new website will continue over the next several months. The 300 webpages that have been migrated to-date account for 80% of all traffic to the city website. Content on both the new and old websites will be maintained until all of the designated webpages have been migrated over to the new website. The old website will eventually be retired in early 2024 once content migration is complete.

item.title: Area Commission Training Announcement: Strategic Planning
item.description:
Strategic Planning for Area Commissions

An Area Commission's Smart Roadmap of Action 

 

The Department of Neighborhoods in partnership with the Soup from A Stone’s, Sharon Ware will host an in-depth training on Strategic Planning for Area Commissions!

The Area Commissioners will face increased economic and social issues in their communities. Strategic planning is instrumental in mapping the next steps of an organization and identifying the best tools for area commissioners.

Participants will develop understanding of the importance of a timeline-roadmap of key goals and the mining of community assets for engagement building. The implementation of goals can incorporate strategic partnerships and collaborations.

Learning objectives will include:

  • Build a one year Area Commission roadmap of area commission goals
  • Utilize community asset mapping to accomplish goals
  • How to request specific partnerships and collaboration needs
  • Finding community best practices
  • How to work smarter and not harder with partnerships

Please join us on Saturday, July 29th, 10:00 – 11:30 AM for a virtual area commission training via WebEx. The WebEx link will be sent to registered participants in a separate email. item.title: Learn About Us: New American Initiative, My Brother’s Keeper Village, Commission on Black Girls
item.description:
Area Commission Training

Topic: New American Initiative, My Brother’s Keeper Village, Commission on Black Girls

The Department of Neighborhoods is inviting you to learn about the New American Initiative, My Brother’s Keeper Village and the Commission on Black Girls!

The WebEx link will be sent to registered participants in a separate email. This is part of the Department of Neighborhoods’ Area Commission Training Series.

The New American Initiative empowers all immigrants and refugees living in Columbus by providing access to City services and programs that help improve the quality of their lives. The initiative advances civic engagement, community awareness and allows immigrants and refugees to become active, productive, and equitable residents of Columbus.

The Commission on Black Girls is dedicated to enriching the lives of Black girls and ensuring that they have opportunities to thrive without the disruption of systemic barriers that have traditionally impacted Black girls.  The Commission strives to provide resources, and advocacy for programs and policies cultivating an environment where Black girls can realize their full potential.

My Brother's Keeper Village leads a national call to action to address systemic barriers, build safe and supportive communities where boys and young men of color are valued and have clear pathways to opportunity.

item.title: Opportunity City: Happy Pride and Summer Fun in Columbus
item.description:
Happy Pride, Columbus!

Our city really comes alive in the summer as we kick off Pride Month and a whole host of family-friendly events like the Jazz & Ribs Fest and Red, White & BOOM!

At a time when the LGBTQ+ community is under relentless attack by state legislators and a vocal minority of extremists, know that Columbus is fully committed to offering a safe and welcoming place for everyone to call home. And, above all else, we reject hate in all its forms.

Let’s continue to uplift one another and come together, as a community, to celebrate the rich and beautiful diversity of our LGBTQ+ neighbors. That is why I, along with hundreds of city employees, will be marching in the 42nd annual Stonewall Pride March on Saturday, June 17. I look forward to seeing so many of you there at what has become the Midwest’s second-largest Pride event of the year.

Sincerely,

Mayor Andy Ginther

Short North Safety Successes

We’re cracking down on violence in the Short North by introducing a number of enhanced safety measures, including an increased police presence and round-the-clock surveillance. I am pleased to report that we’ve seen great success with four back-to-back weekends of improved safety and security. At the same time, we continue to expand our focus on safety city-wide with Operation Moonlight, a comprehensive, data-driven approach that’ll once again place up to 40 additional officers in high-visibility areas during key times throughout the summer. I am also happy to announce the return of our successful Safe Streets program, deploying uniformed bike officers across Columbus neighborhoods to foster open dialogue and trust with the community while conducting enforcement activities to keep our residents safe. 

City of Columbus Investing Over $20 Million in Summer Youth Programming

It is our collective responsibility to invest in our youth 24/7/365, but doing so is particularly important during the summer when they need access to opportunities that keep them safe, active and engaged. That is why the city is investing $20.1 million in summer youth programming this year, including $8.9 million to more than 90 community organizations that submitted funding requests as part of an open, competitive application process. Requests were evaluated based on their potential to:

  • Reduce youth violence,
  • Improve workforce readiness,
  • Connect youth with education and employment,
  • And provide academic enrichment.

View the full list of awardees on the city website, and be sure to sign up for one of these fantastic summer programs while slots are still available.

Construction of Affordable Housing Continues Across Columbus

Last week, I announced the city’s largest single-year capital budget totaling $1.74 billion, paving the way for both new and improved public safety and neighborhood infrastructure – like a new Hilltop police substation and Northside fire station, sidewalks, street resurfacing, utilities and more.

This includes $50 million for affordable housing and home preservation projects, propelling us forward in our continuing journey to make Columbus more affordable for more families. These investments, along with updating the city’s zoning code, are all part of my multi-pronged, regional housing strategy.

See below for a few notable examples of affordable housing success stories:

Bretton Woods Apartments
National Church Residences (Currently accepting applications)

A 62-unit mixed-income senior housing community with wraparound supportive services.

Maple Meadows Apartments
Homeport (Currently accepting applications)

A 56-unit multi-family property offering a variety of apartments of different sizes.

Starling Yard
Woda Cooper Companies, Inc., Franklinton Development Association (Under construction)

A 45-unit apartment complex at the former site of Starling Middle School.

Touchstone Field Place
Community Housing Network (Fully occupied)

100 units offering safe, permanent, supportive housing to individuals who struggle with homelessness, mental illness and substance use.

Columbus Hosts the U.S. Conference of Mayors

As first vice president of the U.S. Conference of Mayors, I was pleased to welcome over 200 of my fellow mayors and city managers to Columbus for our annual meeting. I had the opportunity to learn from my peers and exchange a variety of best practices during our many meaningful discussions. I am particularly proud of the hospitality our community showed our visitors while they were in town, and I am grateful that Columbus continues to remain a top destination for hosting large-scale global events. In fact, our world-renowned hospitality is what brings more than 42 million visitors to our city each year, generating $6.6 billion in direct spend among our local businesses. Let’s keep the momentum going!

item.title: The Commission on Black Girls hosts Free Screening of The Little Mermaid
item.description:
The Commission on Black Girls hosts Free Community Screening of The Little Mermaid

 

The Commission on Black Girls

Join us for a Showing of The Little Mermaid 

“Be the Hero of your Own Story”

Tickets are Complimentary

Hundreds of young Black girls across the nation saw themselves when The Little Mermaid Live-Action Trailer made a big splash earlier this year. Countless videos showed gleeful Black girls in awe and amazement as they watched an Ariel with long beautiful red locs and cinnamon skin mesmerize their screens. These reactions reaffirmed that Black girls need to see positive representations in media and film.

In alignment with the protections found within the CROWN Act and the need to support the positive representation of Black girls and women in media and film, The Commission on Black Girls would like to show girls that they can be the heroines of their own stories, as well as empower advocacy behind changing the portrayal of Black women and girls in film, television and other forms of media. 125 complimentary tickets are available on a first come, first serve basis.

item.title: Opportunity City: Black History Month, gun violence reductions and more
item.description:
Hello, Columbus!

It has been a busy beginning to 2023.

For starters, we kicked off the year with a Career and Resource Fair. I am proud to share that we had over 400 visitors stop by to learn more about employment opportunities with the City of Columbus. If you were not able to attend, there are still several positions available. I encourage anyone interested in a career with the city to create a job profile on our Civil Service website.

Meanwhile, February marks the annual observance of Black History Month, an opportunity to come together as a community to celebrate, honor and reflect upon the history and achievements of Black Americans. There are plenty of special events on the horizon, including Columbus City Council’s Poindexter Award Ceremony on Feb. 17. I encourage everyone to attend and to check out the Black History Month events planned in Columbus and across Central Ohio.

And while we seem to be getting a break from winter weather at the moment, our Snow Warriors are always vigilant and ready to tackle whatever the season throws our way. I look forward to the arrival of warmer temperatures in the coming weeks and seeing all that the new year will bring to our city.

Sincerely,

Mayor Andy Ginther

Crime stats shows Comprehensive Neighborhood Safety Strategy is working

In 2022, Columbus saw a 33% drop in homicides over 2021 – the largest-single percentage drop among the 20-largest U.S. cities. Additionally, Columbus saw a decrease in robberies, burglaries, felonious assaults and rape. This, of course, would not be possible without the hard work and diligence of our public safety personnel and first responders, who, through our updated Comprehensive Neighborhood Safety Strategy, are taking on violence and addressing its root causes using a holistic approach. We know that there is still more to do, and we will continue to invest in the most innovative, creative and effective programs to bring down violence even further and make Columbus the safest big city in America.

City partnering with U.S. Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives to reduce gun violence

Despite homicides in Columbus going down, gun violence remains a devastating problem. In fact, nearly 90% of homicides in Columbus last year involved a firearm. In a collaborative effort with the U.S. Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF), Columbus Division of Police and the City Attorney’s Office, we are working diligently to make Columbus a safer community.

These efforts include $5 million toward tools and technologies to expand our participation in the National Integrated Ballistic Information Network, the only interstate automated ballistic imaging network in the United States. This expansion will allow us to provide actionable investigative leads in a timely fashion.

We also plan to hire two additional special assistant U.S. attorneys.

Finally, we are collaborating with the ATF and other law enforcement partners to create a Regional Crime Gun Intelligence Center to further address violent gun crimes using a broader approach.

In addition to enforcement, there are prevention and intervention tactics, such as youth programming and mental health and addiction services, which will soon be housed within the Office of Violence Prevention - a centralized clearinghouse that will streamline and coordinate the city’s safety responses in a holistic fashion.

Share your feedback on the city's website

The City of Columbus will soon begin work on updating and redesigning its website, columbus.gov, and we want to hear from you!

Take a short, simple survey to tell us what you would like to see in terms of design, navigation, new features and more. Our survey takes less than 10 minutes to complete and will help to ensure a better digital experience for all.

When: Saturday, February 25th

Where: The Reeb Center, 280 Reeb Avenue

Time: 10:00 – 11:30 AM 

Training Description: Since 2010, Columbus started on an accelerated growth trajectory that would be the envy of most communities in the Midwest. Between 2010 and 2021, our metropolitan region added 250,000 residents while the rest of Ohio lost 5,500. The last decennial census revealed the City of Columbus grew at the fastest pace in 70 years and numerically, it was the largest increase in people in a 10 year period in our city’s history. This fast paced presentation takes a deep dive into the past 10 years with use of maps, charts, and data to bring the participants to a common understanding of the city we now share. We will look into the history of redlining, highway building, urban renewal and busing to provide a template for how the city continues to evolve and suggest that while history does not repeat itself, it does rhyme.

Please register for this training by using the RSVP link below. 

https://app.smartsheet.com/b/form/1109fbf29c8e41c99409733a1e175b29

For more information, please contact David Hooie at 614-645-7343 or via email at dehooie@columbus.gov.

We look forward to seeing you on February 25th.

Please join us to celebrate and honor the legacy of the Reverend Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. at the annual City of Columbus MLK Day March and Program.
Be inspired by Mayor Andrew J. Ginther and central Ohio’s Luke Fedlam and recording artist Nia Allen plus more dynamic speakers. This event is free and open to the public.

Monday, January 16, 2023
March begins at 4:30 p.m.

Luke Fedlam


Luke Fedlam is a partner at the law firm of Porter Wright here in Columbus, where he leads the sports law practice group.  He is a nationally known thought-leader, speaker and author on the business of sports and protecting athletes. A Life Member of Alpha Phi Alpha Fraternity, Incorporated, Luke currently services as the Chapter President of Alpha Rho Lambda Chapter, Alpha’s Alumni Chapter here in Columbus.  Outside of work, Luke serves the community on the Board of Directors for the Columbus Clippers, the Board of Trustees for Capital University, the Board of Directors for the National Youth Advocate Program, and the Board of Commissioners for the Greater Columbus Sports Commission.

Nia Allen


Nia Allen is a #1 Billboard artist garnering top success with her inspirational hit song “Wait”.   As a sought-after worship leader Nia has led worship for CeCe Winans “Always Sisters Forever Brothers” youth conferences, Women of Faith’s national conferences, Living Proof Live with Beth Moore and the National Worship Leader’s Conference comprised of over 10,000 Worship Leaders from all around the world.

item.title: My Brother's Keeper Grant Opportunity
item.description:
My Brother's Keeper Grant Opportunity

The City of Columbus Department of Neighborhoods My Brother's Keeper is pleased to announce the availability of $300,000 in general revenue grant funding.  MBK Round 3 is intended to support 501(c)(3) charitable nonprofit organizations serving Columbus and Franklin County boys and men of color. 

Applications are due November 18, 2022 @ 11:59pm

Background

President Barack Obama launched My Brother’s Keeper, a call to action to address the persistent opportunity gaps facing boys and young men of color (BYMOC) and to ensure all young people can reach their full potential. Locally, many have responded to the President’s call to action.  The City of Columbus launched MBK Village and engaged hundreds of young men through the annual summit and conference. These events provided insight on a variety of educational and career opportunities as well as summer employment options.  In recent months, the Department of Neighborhoods has consulted with past, current and potential partners and developed a framework that will guide investment and support for an alignment of stakeholders around strategies that would help to close the gap between boys and young men of color and their peers.  Rooted in the idea that we must work together to expand opportunities for BYMOC, the City envisions a reenergized MBK Village that is focused on priorities aligned with MBK’s key milestones and targets barriers to success at the individual, organizational and systemic levels.

Applicant organizations that serve both young men and women will be considered, but they must demonstrate an explicit emphasis on improving outcomes for BYMOC. Additionally, preference will be given to organizations whose programs are made up of at least 50 percent minority male participants attending public schools.

Round 3 demonstration grants will help project teams test ideas and learn what works to improve high school graduation rates and help participants demonstrate proficient  professional skills to meet the requirements of the Ohio Means Jobs Readiness Seals.

Guidelines

MBK Grant will utilize SmartSheet online application process.  All applications must be submitted online.

Click Here to Apply
